- `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` drives the real exported `checkAuthorIdentity` gate and pins: `pi@local` accepted only via the allow-list, arbitrary foreign email refused, empty email refused even with `allowForeignAuthor`, sentinels never allow-listed. It reads the real project config, so the added entry participates in its membership/exactness assertions; the entry is not individually pinned by name.
- Verification this session: `wl sync --no-push` merged the inbound worklog data with no author-identity refusal (57 work items updated, 0 comments added, 0 `--allow-foreign-author` usage), so the four previously refused commits (`14e4cc89e`, `273325c35`, `23c315392`, `e8c0011a7`) now merge.

`sorra@thewizardscode.com` is accepted permanently as a permitted worklog-sync author through the project allow-list, while the gate's exact-email, empty-email and sentinel guarantees stay intact and continue to be covered by the existing regression tests.

- **Risk (drift):** no test pins the individual `sorra@` entry; removing it would re-strand sync, but loudly (a gate refusal on the next sync), and the contract-level guarantees stay pinned — accepted.
- **Risk (scope):** further identities must each be a separately reviewed config change, not bundled into this item.
- **Risk (widening):** the allow-list is a project-wide policy widening; it stays bounded because matching is exact-email and empty emails are always refused.

- SA-0MVGSB63F00803HK — precedent: allow-listing `pi@local` with the same bounded, exact-email approach.

# Intake brief — test-slot pool starvation: max_workers=2 runs never probe slots >= 2 even when free

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** bug (framework tooling; no gameplay behaviour change) ·
**Status:** intake complete — non-blocking producer questions recorded in the Appendix.

## Provenance

This is the authoritative tracking item for the defect. It was transferred here
from the AI_Hell store on 2026-11-03 (operator decision) because every affected
file is the SorraAgents framework source (`skill/shared`, `skill/test`,
`docs/dev`). The original AI_Hell item **AH-0MVWS3360005NRYI** — *"Test-suite
semaphore waiter can sit for 100+ min while slots are free"* — carried the intake
brief, the plan and five planned children; the four implementation children are
recreated under this item (the fifth — reconciling the earlier SorraAgents stub
— is satisfied by this transfer itself), and the AI_Hell item and its children
are closed as transferred.
The earlier stub `SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0` (same root cause, no acceptance criteria,
filed from the SA-0MVPUVM8F006270F session) is this item, now enriched with the
ACs and evidence.

## Problem statement

A test-run slot waiter that starts when the host pool is small keeps probing
only the slot indices that existed at that moment, so it can wait out its entire
`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (up to 2 h when the timeout has been raised) while other
processes' slots sit free in the same namespace. Observed twice on 2026-10-31
while driving epic AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG: `implement.py finish` reached the
`run_tests` step, printed "falling back to full scope", then sat in
`hrtimer_nanosleep` for **105 minutes** while 5 of 8 host test slots were free.

## Users (user stories)

- *As an agent finishing a work item*, I need the changed-scope/full-suite gate
  to take a free slot within a bounded time no matter how long I have already
  been waiting, so a green change is not blocked for hours and my session does
  not time out with the work uncommitted.
- *As a producer/release operator*, I need a `slot_busy` verdict to mean the
  pool really was full for the whole wait, so I can tell "retry later" from
  "the waiter is stuck" without inspecting `/proc`.
- *As a framework maintainer*, I need the slot-discovery rule and the maximum
  poll interval pinned by tests, so a future semaphore change cannot silently
  reintroduce this starvation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Bounded acquisition once any slot in the namespace is free.** A
  waiter that began polling when only slots `0..N-1` existed must acquire
  within a documented bound (one poll interval plus one `flock` attempt) as
  soon as **any** slot file in its namespace is free — including slot files
  created by a later, higher-ceiling process. Reproduce with a test that starts
  a `max_workers=2` waiter against an empty namespace, holds slots 0 and 1, then
  creates slots 2–7 after the waiter has been polling; the waiter must acquire
  one of the new slots well inside its timeout.
- **AC2 — Documented maximum poll interval, no unbounded backoff.** The poll
  cadence has a documented maximum interval (today: 50 ms base, jittered
  `[0.5, 1.5]×` when jitter is enabled) and a test pins that a long-waiting
  consumer still observes slots created after it began waiting (many poll
  cycles, not one). No backoff may grow without a documented cap.
- **AC3 — Genuine saturation still reports `slot_busy`.** When every slot in
  the namespace is held for the whole `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, the test skill still
  raises `TestConcurrencyTimeout` carrying the `slot_busy` notice code and the
  existing staggered-retry guidance — the no-slot notice must not be weakened
  or renamed.
- **AC4 — Testing/validation.** New/updated tests cover AC1 (slot created after
  the waiter started), AC2 (max interval pinned; late-created slot observed)
  and AC3 (genuine saturation notice). Tests are hermetic (temporary
  `PI_SEMAPHORE_DIR`, no host-wide pool) and use real subprocesses where the
  behaviour is cross-process; no ad-hoc suite invocations.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** The `process_semaphore` module docstring documents
  the discovery rule, the effective-ceiling rule and the maximum poll interval;
  `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` documents the same and states that
  `slot_busy` means genuine saturation for the whole wait.
- **AC6 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Do not change the configured ceiling.** `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` /
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_FAST` semantics stay as they are
  (`SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` forbids changing the ceiling). This is about
  *discovering* existing capacity, not creating more.
- **A waiter may only use slots another process created.** It must not create
  more slot files than its own `max_workers` (its own ceiling stays a floor it
  guarantees, not a host-wide limit it may exceed).
- **Keep the kernel-`flock` model.** No PID bookkeeping, no stale locks, no
  new daemon; a killed waiter must not hold a slot or a discovery marker.
- **Compose with, do not duplicate, the fairness work.** Arrival ordering
  (FIFO turnstile) is owned by `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI`; this item must not
  implement ordering, and the discovery scan must remain compatible with a
  future ticket layer.
- **Preserve jitter and nested-run isolation.** `SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD` stagger
  and `SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86` `nested_semaphore_dir` isolation must keep working.
- **Fail-fast callers stay fail-fast.** `audit_runner` enters with `timeout=0`;
  a discovery scan must not add blocking work to the first attempt.
- **Framework repo boundaries.** The code lives in this repository's framework
  source (`skill/shared`, `skill/test`, `docs/dev`), which is symlinked as
  `~/.pi/agent/skills`; consumers get it via `scripts/install_pi.sh`. Implementation
  therefore happens in a worktree of this checkout.
- **UK English** throughout.

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — counting semaphore over a pool of slot
  lock files. `_try_acquire_slot()` iterates `range(self.max_workers)` and
  `flock`s the first free file; `max_workers` is resolved **once** in
  `__init__` (explicit arg > `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` > default 6).
  `_ensure_slots()` creates files `0..max_workers-1` for the calling process.
  **A process whose ceiling is 2 therefore never opens slot files 2–7**, even
  when they exist and are unlocked.
- Poll cadence today: `time.sleep(_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS)` = 50 ms, or
  `_jittered_retry_delay()` = `[0.5, 1.5] × 50 ms`. **There is no unbounded
  backoff** — the original "backoff grows without limit" suspicion does not
  match the shipped code; the `range(max_workers)` scan is the defect.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_test_concurrency_slot()` builds a
  `Semaphore` per execution with the lane ceiling (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`,
  default 6 for the full lane; 4 for `test-fast`), `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`
  (default 600 s), `TEST_LOCK_JITTER` (default 0.1) and raises
  `TestConcurrencyTimeout` with the `slot_busy` notice.
- Live evidence: `/run/user/1000/pi-semaphores/test/` contains slot files
  `0`–`7`; `6` and `7` were created at 18:02 while the stuck waiter had been
  polling since 17:25. At 19:15 UTC slots 0, 1, 5 were held and 2, 3, 4, 6, 7
  were free; the waiter owned no lock in `/proc/locks`. The pool ceiling had
  grown from 2 to 8 during the incident as agents with different
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` values joined.
- Impact: three child sessions of AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG timed out at 3600 / 5400
  / 7200 s with work left uncommitted; killing and re-running `finish` was the
  only workaround found (a fresh process resolves a fresh `max_workers`).

## Desired change

1. Make slot discovery dynamic: each acquisition attempt must consider every
   numeric slot file currently present in the namespace directory (not just
   indices below the caller's snapshot ceiling), while never creating files
   beyond the caller's own `max_workers`.
2. Keep the poll cadence bounded and documented (no unbounded backoff); pin the
   maximum interval in the module docstring and in a test.
3. Keep the `slot_busy` notice for genuine saturation and add the regression
   tests described in AC1–AC4.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — replace the `range(max_workers)` probe
  with a namespace scan (numeric slot files), document the discovery rule,
  effective-ceiling rule and maximum poll interval; keep `_ensure_slots()`
  bounded by the caller's `max_workers`.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_process_semaphore.py` — new tests: slot created
  after the waiter started is acquired inside the documented bound; many poll
  cycles still observe late-created slots; max poll interval pinned; waiter
  never creates slots beyond its own `max_workers`.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_concurrency_guard.py` — cross-process regression
  that a low-ceiling waiter uses a higher-index slot created by another
  process.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — no semantic change expected; confirm the
  `slot_busy` notice path is untouched (AC3) and the wrapper still passes the
  lane ceiling through.
- `skill/test/tests/test_test_skill_semaphore.py` — regression: genuinely full
  pool for the whole `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` still yields the `slot_busy` notice
  with stagger guidance.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — document discovery, effective ceiling,
  max poll interval and the meaning of `slot_busy`.

## Related work

- **AH-0MVWS3360005NRYI** (AI_Hell store, `intake_complete`) — *"Test-suite
  semaphore waiter can sit for 100+ min while slots are free"*: the item this
  brief was transferred from. It holds the measured 105-minute stall evidence
  and the AI_Hell-side provenance; it is closed as transferred so the fix is
  written once, here.
- **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (in-progress, `intake_complete`) — test-slot
  **fairness/arrival ordering** (FIFO turnstile) plus dev-push gate reporting.
  Different failure mode (ordering, not discovery); the discovery scan must
  compose with its turnstile and must not implement it.
- **SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z** (critical, `plan_complete`) — owns the changed-scope
  gate classification fields and explicitly forbids changing
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`; this item keeps that constraint.
- **SA-0MVEDOF7A004TSWD** (completed) — staggered-wait jitter; preserved.
- **SA-0MUY6U05F008RG86** (completed) — nested-run semaphore isolation;
  preserved.
- **AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG** — the epic whose child sessions timed out; this item
  is `discovered-from` it.
- **AH-0MVWJYIB4006PZTU** (in-progress, `idea`) — the changed-scope gate
  falling back to full scope in this Vitest repo; it makes this item's symptom
  more frequent (every finish queues a full suite) but is otherwise independent.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: a discovery scan weakens the host ceiling.** Mitigation: only
  *existing* files are probed; the caller still creates at most its own
  `max_workers` slots, and the documented rule states that the effective pool is
  the union of slot files present.
- **Risk: directory scan cost on every 50 ms poll.** Mitigation: a single
  `iterdir()`/`scandir()` of a small directory (≤ ~10 entries); document the
  measured cost in the docstring or a comment.
- **Risk: conflicting ceilings produce surprising total concurrency.** This is
  already true today (the incident's pool grew to 8); the change makes capacity
  *usable*, it does not create it. Recorded as an assumption, not re-litigated
  here (`SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` owns ceiling policy).
- **Risk: scope creep into fairness or ceiling policy.** Mitigation: ordering
  stays with `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI`; ceiling stays untouched; any extra
  opportunity becomes a linked work item.
- **Assumption:** the 105-minute wait was a bounded wait with a raised
  `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (e.g. 7200 s), not an unbounded one — the shipped code
  always has a deadline, and 105 min fits a raised bound plus the 3-attempt
  gate retry loop.
- **Assumption:** `implement.py finish` restarting and succeeding is explained
  by a fresh process resolving a fresh ceiling/slot set, which is consistent
  with the snapshot-ceiling root cause.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

Session: auto-dispatched (`herdr-downtime`, 2026-11-01) — no producer was
present in-session. Questions are recorded with the agent's explicitly
recommended option and a proposed default; they are **non-blocking** because
the brief is complete under the defaults, and each default is a localised
change if the producer prefers otherwise. Producer confirmation is still
requested before planning proceeds past these points.

- **Q1 — How should a waiter discover slots added after it started?**
  (a) scan the namespace directory for numeric slot files on each attempt;
  (b) keep the index scan but adopt
  `max(self.max_workers, highest_existing_index + 1)` as the effective ceiling
  per attempt; (c) re-read `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` on each poll and re-run
  `_ensure_slots()`.
  **Recommended:** (a) — it is the smallest change, needs no env re-read, and
  is correct regardless of which ceiling another process used. **Proposed
  default:** (a). Source: agent recommendation (no interactive reply).
- **Q2 — Cross-repo ownership: which item is authoritative?** *Resolved by
  operator on 2026-11-03:* the item belongs in the SorraAgents store, because the
  code is the framework source. The AI_Hell item **AH-0MVWS3360005NRYI** was
  therefore transferred into this item (`SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0`) — its brief,
  evidence, plan and children moved here and it is closed as transferred. No
  action remains.
- **Q3 — May the `slot_busy` notice semantics change?** (a) no — keep the
  notice and its `slot_busy` code exactly as shipped, adding only the
  regression test; (b) extend the notice to distinguish "pool churned" from
  "pool full" (would touch the notice contract consumed by
  `implement.py finish` and the pre-push hook).
  **Recommended:** (a) — the notice is consumed by the gate classification
  (`GATE_FAILURE_SLOT_CONTENTION`) and its consumers are outside this item's
  scope. **Proposed default:** (a). Source: agent recommendation; evidence
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` `_NOTICE_SLOT_BUSY`.
## Related work (automated report)

_Note (intake):_ the automated matches below keyed on generic tokens (`ac1`, `slot`) and surfaced HUD-slot and thruster items plus gameplay docs; none of them concerns the test-slot semaphore. The manual **Related work** section above is authoritative.

- **AH-0MVVJRFDV007OI49** – HUD/slot agreement tests and reporting fixture (completed)
- **AH-0MVVJRRN10038VFR** – HUD six-slot budget and non-slot row marking (completed)

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+399 more)

# GitHub closes the idle SSH connection during the pre-push full-suite gate

Parent: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** — this is the concrete root cause behind one of the
"transient push-transport closes" that item asks us to retry. Retrying does not
help on its own: the connection is dropped with a *deterministic* trigger
(SSH idling for the duration of the suite), so every attempt fails the same way
and the agent loops, burning a full suite run each time.

## Problem

`.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full` **after** `git` has
established the SSH connection to `github.com` and **before** the ref update.
The hook produces no SSH traffic for the whole run (measured 11 min warm, 35 min
cold on this host), so the remote closes the idle connection:

```
pre-push: full-suite gate for dev/main push — running run_tests.py --scope full ...
Connection to github.com closed by remote host.
pre-push: full suite green (cached runs make repeat pushes cheap)
pre-push: mirrored gate cache entry 96dd15da... into .worklog/cache
```

The gate reports **green**, the cache entries are mirrored — and the push never
lands: `git push` exits without updating the ref and `origin/dev` is unchanged.
Observed 2026-10-31 on two consecutive attempts from
`wl-LP-0MVWIA33O004RKP7-…` in `llm-manager`; `~/.ssh/config` sets no
`ServerAliveInterval`/`TCPKeepAlive`.

Impact:

- A green full-suite run is discarded, so the most expensive part of the push is
  paid repeatedly; because each retry rebases onto a moved `dev`, the tree
  changes and the suite cache misses, so retries are *cold*.
- The output reads as success ("full suite green") while the push silently did
  not happen — the misleading signal is arguably worse than a hard failure.

## Workaround that worked (not a fix)

```bash
GIT_SSH_COMMAND="ssh -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20 -o TCPKeepAlive=yes" \
  WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/dev
# -> d925d89d..877a6512  HEAD -> dev
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A dev push whose pre-push gate runs longer than the remote's idle timeout
      succeeds, with no manual `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` override by the agent.
- [ ] Keepalives are configured in a way that survives a fresh clone/worktree
      (e.g. set by the hook or by `implement.py`'s push, not only in one
      operator's `~/.ssh/config`).
- [ ] When the ref update is still lost after a green suite, the push reports a
      distinct, loud failure (not "full suite green" followed by silence), and
      distinguishes "suite red" from "transport lost".
- [ ] A regression test covers the transport-loss path (simulated closed
      connection) and asserts the distinct failure classification.

## Notes

- `SA-0MVU0IS9S006BFE3` / `SA-0MVUTXJ4300301ZN` (push must run from the worktree)
  is a separate defect; both were hit in the same session. This item is only the
  transport side.
- Related: `~/.ssh/config` on the multi-agent host currently has no
  `ServerAlive*` settings at all.

# implement.py Key Files gate misses the bold-inside-heading form

**Discovered from:** RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8 (tce-the-rising implement run, 2026-10-31). That RISE item was filed during `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` and is deleted once this item exists (producer decision Q1 = re-file here).

**Headline:** The Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate in `implement.py` parses only
`## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)` and a bare `**Key Files:**` line, so a
work item whose section is written `## **Key Files:**` (bold marker nested in an
H2/H3) yields no key files, dirty-file relevance becomes unjudgeable, and
`implement.py start` aborts on a dirty checkout even when every dirty path is
unrelated. Make the heading matcher form-agnostic and lock it down with
regression tests.

## Problem statement

`_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` matches
`#{1,6}\s*Key Files.*` (heading) **or** `\*\*Key Files:?\*\*.*` (bold line) — but
not the combination `## **Key Files:**`, because after the `## ` prefix the next
token is `**`, not `Key Files`. `extract_key_files_from_description()` then
returns `[]`, `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` reports *"no Key Files section in
the work item description — cannot judge dirty-file relevance"*, and
`phase_start` takes the conservative abort-and-ask branch even though the
description does list key files and the dirty paths demonstrably do not overlap
them. The gate's conservative default is correct; it is being tripped by a
parser gap rather than by a real risk.

## Evidence

Reproduced in this session against the installed skill tree
(`~/.pi/agent/skills` → `SorraAgents/skill`):

| form | `extract_key_files_from_description` |
|---|---|
| `## Key Files` | `['a/b.ts', 'tests/c.test.ts']` |
| `## Key Files (predicted)` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `**Key Files:**` | `['a/b.ts']` |
| `## **Key Files:**` | `[]` |
| `### **Key Files:**` | `[]` |

- **Corpus prevalence (consumer store):** 9 of 386 items in the
  `tce-the-rising` store use the bold-inside-heading form — the face-off tie
  epic parent RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU and its eight children
  (RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX, RISE-0MVRMI7GR006QH44, RISE-0MVRMI9F0007HXBW,
  RISE-0MVRMIB7Z008P1HB, RISE-0MVRMID1B0098HAY, RISE-0MVRMIF0T008A72W,
  RISE-0MVRMIGXS0073HDX, RISE-0MVRMIISC009TXYX). For comparison: 297 items use
  a plain heading, 52 a bare bold line, 28 none.
- **Observed stall:** `implement.py drive RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU` aborted on child
  RISE-0MVRMI5XD002EDKX (Key Files: `tests/the-rising/risingMatchHarness.ts`,
  `tests/the-rising/TheRisingRules.test.ts`) although the only dirty paths were
  six untracked `standups/*.md` files — zero overlap, i.e. exactly the
  documented "proceed, leave the dirty files untouched" case. The operator
  worked around it by pre-creating the worktree and running `start` from inside
  it (where the main-checkout gate is skipped by design).
- **No direct test coverage** of `extract_key_files_from_description`,
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files` or `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` exists under
  `skill/implement/tests/`, so this class of gap is invisible to the suite.
- The framework does **not** emit the H2-wrapped form itself:
  `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` (`_parse_key_files_section`,
  `validate_key_files_format`) and `skill/plan/SKILL.md` use a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line, so both families of form must keep working.

## Users

- **Implement-skill agent (primary)**: "When I start an item whose Key Files
  section is written `## **Key Files:**`, I want `start` to read those paths and
  let me proceed when the dirty files are unrelated, so I do not have to
  hand-work around a gate that already has the information it needs."
- **Producer / operator (secondary)**: "When a downtime run dispatches a child
  session, I want `start` to proceed or abort for a real reason, so unattended
  runs do not stall on a parsing bug."
- **Framework maintainer**: "I want every accepted Key Files heading form
  covered by a table-driven test, so a future edit to the extractor cannot
  silently drop a form."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `extract_key_files_from_description()` returns the listed paths for
  any `Key Files` heading regardless of emphasis, parenthetical qualifier or
  case: `## **Key Files:**`, `### **Key Files:**`, `## **Key Files (predicted):**`,
  `#### key files`, asserted by a table-driven unit test in
  `skill/implement/tests/`.
- **AC2** — Every currently supported form keeps working, asserted in the same
  table: `## Key Files`, `## Key Files (predicted)`, `### Key Files`, and a bare
  `**Key Files:**` line; plus the tolerant bare-marker variants —
  `  **Key Files:**` (indented/whitespace) and `**Key Files**` (no colon).
- **AC3** — `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()` proceeds (`can_proceed: true`)
  when the description uses `## **Key Files:**` and the dirty paths do not
  overlap those entries, and still aborts (`can_proceed: false`) when a dirty
  path does overlap, or when the description has no Key Files section at all.
- **AC4** — Extraction still stops at the end of the Key Files section: a
  following `#`/`##`/`###` heading or standalone bold section marker terminates
  the list, so prose lines and acceptance-criteria bullets never leak in as
  paths (regression guard for the SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2 defect class).
- **AC5** — A regression test demonstrates the defect before the fix (red on the
  current implementation, green after), and the end-to-end path is verified:
  `implement.py start` on a `## **Key Files:**` item with only unrelated dirty
  paths creates the worktree, leaves the dirty files untouched and records the
  decision in a work-item comment.
- **AC6** — The gate's safety properties are preserved: no
  stash/commit/revert of dirty files, and abort-and-ask still fires for "no Key
  Files section" and for any overlap.
- **AC7** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments and docstrings in `implement.py` and the accepted-forms
  list in `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree
  gate, SA-0MV0NSOGE000OSMR) plus the project README and any relevant wiki or
  docs site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope is `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`** plus its tests and docs
  (producer decision Q2 = A). The two sibling parsers — `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  and `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — are fixed by linked follow-up
  items (below), not here.
- **The gate stays conservative.** No Key Files section, or any overlapping
  dirty path, must still abort and ask. Nothing here may turn the gate into a
  whitelist or relax "never stash/commit/revert the user's work".
- **Must not regress existing forms.** The new matcher may be more tolerant but
  never stricter: an item that starts cleanly today must still start cleanly.
- **Minimal surface.** No new configuration knob or environment variable.
- **UK English** in comments, docstrings and docs.

## Existing state

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE` (~line 1671),
  `extract_key_files_from_description()` (~1676),
  `dirty_file_matches_key_files()` (~1712), `classify_dirty_tree_relevance()`
  (~1742), and the `phase_start` call site (~5993) that turns a
  `can_proceed: false` verdict into the dirty-worktree abort.
- The extractor's loop already terminates on a `#`-heading line or a non-bullet
  line starting with `**`; only the initial heading match is wrong. A new
  matcher must not let the matched heading's own bold marker look like the
  section end.
- `skill/implement/tests/` has suites for the start/finish gates but none that
  exercises the Key Files extractor or the relevance classifier.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate
  section) enumerates the three supported forms and needs the tolerant list.

## Desired change

1. Replace the two-branch heading regex with one form-agnostic matcher: an
   optional H1–H6 prefix, an optional `**` bold marker, `Key Files`, an optional
   parenthetical qualifier and optional closing `**`/`:`, matched
   case-insensitively — while still requiring `Key Files` to be the first
   content token (so `## Notes on Key Files` stays unmatched unless it matches
   today).
2. Keep the section terminator and the bullet/backtick path parsing unchanged
   (including `path → note`).
3. Add the table-driven tests (AC1–AC5) and the end-to-end `start` regression.
4. Update the docstring/comment and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — form-agnostic `_KEY_FILES_HEADING_RE`,
  extractor terminator/docstrings; classifier branches unchanged.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_key_files_extraction.py` — new table-driven tests
  for the accepted forms, the terminator behaviour and
  `classify_dirty_tree_relevance` proceed/abort decisions.
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — accepted-forms list in the
  Key-Files-aware dirty-tree gate section.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — over/under-matching:** tightening "first content token" could make a
  heading that matches today (e.g. `## Key Files and notes`) stop matching.
  Keep the match at least as wide as today; assert the old forms in the table.
- **Risk — terminator drift:** after accepting the new form the loop must not
  treat the matched heading's own `**` as a section end.
- **Risk — untestable "it works now" claims:** the AC5 end-to-end check needs a
  deliberately dirty main checkout, so it must leave the dirty files untouched
  and clean up after itself (or exercise the classifier/`phase_start` seam
  directly).
- **Assumption:** the H2-wrapped form is agent-authored markdown, not framework
  output — so the fix belongs in the tolerant parser, not in the plan skill's
  emitter.
- **Scope-creep guard:** the plan/audit parsers are separate items (below);
  anything further discovered goes to `discovered-from` items, not this fix.

## Related work

- **SA-0MV0NSOGE000OSMR** — Allow implement.py start to create a clean worktree
  when main checkout is dirty: introduced the gate and the three-form parser;
  this item fixes its blind spot.
- **SA-0MUYEV5AO006V0HK** — project-local skill extensions / dirty-tree
  exemptions (the other documented relaxation path of the same gate).
- **SA-0MTYMD1NQ009R6W2** — `plan_helpers._parse_key_files_section` did not stop
  at Markdown headings (same failure family: section-boundary parsing).
- **SA-0MTYP6T2I00396J7** — generated `standups/` output not gitignored: the
  source of the six dirty files in the reproduction.
- **SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ** — the previous framework fix discovered from a
  tce-the-rising implement run (disposition precedent for this re-filing).
- **RISE-0MVPAGZP0003EKZU** — Face-off tie epic whose children carry the
  `## **Key Files:**` form and whose drive run hit the abort.

## Linked follow-up items (producer decision Q2 = B and C)

- **Follow-up 1 — plan parser:** `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py`
  `_parse_key_files_section` / `validate_key_files_format` should accept the same
  heading forms so plan validation does not report a missing/empty Key Files
  section for a validly-written description.
- **Follow-up 2 — audit parser:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`'s Key
  Files extraction (`^#{0,4}\s*Key Files.*?$`) has the same blind spot, which
  omits the item's files from the Phase 2 file-scope manifest. Either fix it
  locally or extract one shared, heading-aware Key Files helper consumed by
  implement/plan/audit.

Both are filed with `discovered-from:<this item>`; their SA ids are recorded in
this item's comments.

## Appendix — clarifying questions & answers

Interview raised on RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8 (comment `RISE-C0MVWO1N400000N41`),
answered by the producer in-session on 2026-10-31. Answers are transcribed
verbatim.

- **Q1 — Which worklog/store carries the fix?**
  **Answer (producer): "A - delete this when filed"** → the fix is re-filed in
  the SorraAgents worklog as this item (with `discovered-from:RISE-0MVWARX2M001ZXS8`)
  and the RISE item is deleted once this item exists. Recommended option A was
  accepted. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q2 — How wide is the parser fix?**
  **Answer (producer): "A, with B and C as linked follow-ups"** →
  `implement.py` only in this item; the plan parser (B) and audit parser (C) are
  filed as linked follow-up items rather than folded in. Recommended option A
  was accepted. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- **Q3 — Which heading variants must be accepted?**
  **Answer (producer): "B + C"** → accept any `Key Files` heading regardless of
  emphasis, parenthetical qualifier or case (B), **and** tolerate whitespace /
  colon variants of the bare bold marker (C). Recommended option was B; the
  producer widened it to B+C, reflected in AC1/AC2. Source: interactive reply,
  this session.
- **Q (research, answered by inspection) — Does the framework emit the
  H2-wrapped form?** No: `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py:127-160` and
  `skill/plan/SKILL.md:181,306` specify a bare `**Key Files:**` line; the
  H2-wrapped form in the consumer store was authored into descriptions directly.
- **Q (research, answered by inspection) — How many items are affected in the
  consumer store?** 9 of 386 (`tce-the-rising`), all inside the face-off tie
  epic. Evidence: SQL scan of that store's `workitems.description`.

# Release gate (merge-dev-to-main.sh) discards the runner JSON, so a dev→main release cannot say why the suite gate failed

Discovered-from: **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (during `/skill:plan`).

## Problem

`skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` runs the full-suite release
gate as:

```bash
if python3 "$TEST_RUNNER" --scope full --strict-git-env 2>&1; then
```

The runner's machine-readable result is never requested and the exit code is
the only signal, so a slot-contention expiry (`slot_busy`), a killed suite
(`killed`) and a genuine red suite all produce the same message: "Full test
suite failed on the merged dev→main tree — the release is blocked." The
operator cannot tell "fix the code" from "wait for a slot / raise
`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`", and a release attempt can burn hours of queue wait before
failing indistinguishably from a real regression.

The pre-push hook gets the equivalent fix under **SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI** (its
AC2/AC3); this item is the same defect on the release path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The release gate consumes the runner's machine-readable result and reports the same `gate_reason=<code>` vocabulary the pre-push hook uses.
- [ ] A slot-contention or killed-run failure prints a distinct message with the remediation hint (wait then re-run, or raise `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`), while a red suite keeps its current message.
- [ ] The gate still fails closed (non-zero exit, no release) in every failure case, and `SHIP_TEST_SKIP=1` still bypasses it.
- [ ] A hermetic test (following `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py`) pins the classification for slot contention, killed and red-suite cases.

## Notes

- Reuse the shared classifier introduced by SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI rather than a second copy; this item is deliberately **not** a child of it so the release path can ship independently.
- UK English throughout.

data.description:
# Live-repo guard fails a run when a concurrent `wl sync` moves `refs/heads/worklog/data`

## Target outcome

A full-suite run must not be failed — and must not lose its green cache entry —
because another agent's concurrent `wl sync` moved the Worklog data ref.

**Observed** while finishing SA-0MVQQ9KZO0010XXS (2026-11-01):

```
run_tests.py --scope full → success: false
live-repo mutation detected: … moved ref refs/heads/worklog/data:
  0067d646089788ee530ff8856bd481d7bd1cd7c7 -> 96ea6f021c940ed2374e353de9f1df84f9438e6d
  (in the worktree AND in the main checkout)
```

Every test suite passed (`suites.all.returncode == 0`, 835/835 node tests, pytest
green), but the outer guard's verdict forces `success: false`, so no green
full-suite cache entry is written, and `implement.py finish`'s gate reports
"infrastructure reason" with no structured failures.

## Root cause

`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` excludes `refs/worklog/*` (`WORKLOG_REF_PREFIX`)
from the mutation surface, but the Worklog data ref also lives — and moves —
under `refs/heads/worklog/data`. Concurrent `wl sync` (sibling `implement.py
finish` pushes, the herdr downtime worker) moves it while any suite runs, so the
guard reports it as a mutation of the guarded checkout.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Excluded as concurrency churn.** `refs/heads/worklog/data`
  (and the `refs/heads/worklog/` namespace generally) is excluded from the
  live-repo mutation surface, derived from the ref name (never a work-item
  pattern), reported instead as an informational note.
- [ ] **AC2 — Regression pinned.** A test snapshots a fixture checkout, moves
  `refs/heads/worklog/data` externally, and asserts `_detect_live_repo_mutation`
  reports no mutation (note only).
- [ ] **AC3 — Suite-caused data movement still fails.** A suite that itself
  commits to `refs/heads/worklog/data` remains a mutation (the exclusion is
  provenance independent only if the guard cannot distinguish; if it cannot,
  document the blind spot explicitly in `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`).

## Key Files

data.description:
## Goal

As the operator, I want the 2026-10-31 test-slot starvation fix proved shut with post-fix
measurements, and the remaining cross-consumer duplicate-suite vector removed, so that no agent
session loses minutes queueing for a 1–3 s test run and no two consumers pay twice for the same
full suite.

## Problem statement

The fast-lane fix (`SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`, shipped `a2659c38` on 2026-10-31T23:21) delivered the
separate `test-fast` semaphore namespace, the re-derived `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT = 6` and
the `slot_wait_seconds`/`slot_lane` reporting. Two gaps remain from the original RCA item
(`LP-0MVWZ8QPY000UVQM`, llm repo — closed as superseded by `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`):

1. **No post-fix measurement.** Its AC5 ("median blocked time per work item falls materially below
   ~10 min/test call; evidence recorded") was never executed. A preliminary scan of the 30 pi
   session logs touched since `a2659c38` found 12 `slot_wait_seconds` samples, all `0.00 s`, and
   zero `queued N s for a <lane>-lane slot` notices — encouraging, but too small a sample to close
   the question, and it says nothing about the two dominant wait categories (`implement finish` and
   the dev-push full-suite gate), which appear as `wait_for_job` blocks, not `run_tests.py` JSON.
2. **Verdicts are not reusable across consumers.** `run_cached()` keys on either the loose worktree
   fingerprint or — when the caller passes an explicit would-be-commit tree SHA — on
   `fingerprint_kind="tree"`. `implement.py` finish passes a tree SHA; the pre-push gate, the test
   CLI and the audit path pass nothing and therefore keep historical loose-worktree keys
   (`docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` § "Explicit-fingerprint override" says so outright). A green
   full-suite verdict therefore cannot be carried between the pre-commit staged tree and the pushed
   commit, so a dev push re-executes the full suite even when an identical tree was validated
   minutes earlier.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — needs evidence, not anecdotes, that the critical starvation fix worked:
  *As the operator, I want a recorded p50/p90/max of post-fix slot wait so I can close the RCA with
  data rather than with the fix's assertion.*
- **Agent session** — *As an agent pushing to `dev`, I want the gate to reuse a green verdict for
  the tree I am pushing so my push does not cost a second 7–9 minute suite run.*

## Existing state

- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` + `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`: two lanes
  (`test`, `test-fast`), ceilings 6 and 4, `slot_wait_seconds`/`slot_lane`/`slot_lanes` reported,
  `queued N s for a <lane>-lane slot` notice at ≥ 1 s.
- `skill/test_cache.py`: `compute_tree_state(index_file)` → `git write-tree` SHA;
  `run_cached(..., fingerprint=<sha>)` keys lookup and store with
  `FINGERPRINT_KIND_TREE`; `query_cached()` stays worktree-only by design.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`: finish no longer runs a full suite at all — it defers to
  the dev-push gate (`SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`) and passes the tree SHA for its changed-scope verdict
  (`SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB`).
- `.githooks/pre-push` (SorraAgents, v3): full-suite gate runs
  `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` with **no** `--fingerprint`, i.e. worktree-keyed.
  It also **ignores the pushed `local_sha`** entirely (only `remote_ref` selects the gate), so the
  suite validates whatever the checkout happens to contain — there is no pushed-commit guard in
  this hook yet (the `llm` repo's diverged v4 hook has one: `LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9`).
  `.githooks/pre-push.v2` (installed into other projects) deliberately has no suite gate, so it
  needs no change. Per-repo hooks diverge: `~/projects/llm/.githooks/pre-push` is a separate v4
  variant with its own pushed-commit guard and a `--project-root` argument.

## Desired change

1. Re-measure the post-fix wait distribution and record it (with the method) in this item.
2. Give the pre-push full-suite gate a pushed-commit guard and a tree-keyed fingerprint (plumbed
   through the runner CLI), so the gate measures the tree it pushes and its verdict lands in the
   same namespace as the finish gate's, and is reused when the tree matches.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Post-fix re-measurement recorded.** A reproducible analysis (commands/script cited in the item)
   over every pi session log covering at least 24 h after `a2659c38` (or all sessions since
   2026-10-31T23:21 if fewer) reports, per wait category — (a) `run_tests.py` slot wait, (b)
   `implement finish`, (c) dev-push full-suite gate — the call count and p50/p90/max wall clock.
   Pass: no run reports `slot_wait_seconds > 120 s`, partial-run (`test-fast`) p90 < 30 s, and no
   `queued N s` notice ≥ 30 s. Any miss is recorded honestly and filed as follow-up work, not
   smoothed over.
2. **The pre-push gate keys on the pushed tree.** The gate first adds the pushed-commit guard this
   hook currently lacks (pushed `local_sha` must equal the checkout's `HEAD` and the tree must be
   clean, with a loud refusal naming the commit, the HEAD, the tree path and the recovery step —
   the `llm` v4 hook's wording is the precedent), then computes that commit's tree SHA and passes
   it explicitly, so the verdict is stored and looked up with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`. When the
   guard fails or the tree SHA cannot be computed the gate refuses rather than falling back to a
   loose worktree key (fail-closed, matching the cache's provenance contract).
3. **Cross-consumer reuse proven.** A test demonstrates that a full-suite verdict recorded for tree
   *T* by one caller (finish gate / tree-keyed `run_cached`) is served as a cache hit to the
   pre-push gate for the same *T*, and that a different tree misses. The gate reports cache
   hit/miss (and the reused entry's age) in its stderr/JSON output so a served verdict is visible.
4. **Runner CLI surface + docs.** `run_tests.py` accepts an explicit tree fingerprint for
   `--scope full` (the parameter already threads through `run_suite`/`run_all`), documented in
   `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`; `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` and the hook's header comment are
   updated — the "callers that pass nothing keep worktree keys … (test-skill CLI, audit, pre-push)"
   sentence must no longer describe the pre-push gate.
5. **Tests.** Deterministic tests cover: the gate computes and passes the pushed tree SHA; a
   same-tree second run is a hit; a different tree is a miss; fail-closed when `HEAD != local_sha`,
   when the tree is dirty, or when the tree SHA is unavailable; worktree-keyed callers' cache keys
   are unchanged byte for byte. Existing cache/provenance, finish-gate-tree and pre-push hook tests
   stay green.
6. **Rollout is explicit, not implicit.** The item records that the `llm` repo's diverged v4 hook
   needs its own change (follow-up item), and that `pre-push.v2` consumers are unaffected.
7. **Testing/validation criterion.** Every new behaviour above is exercised by an automated test
   that fails before the change and passes after it, executed through the test skill.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant docs-site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Repository scope:** implementation lands in this repo only (`skill/test_cache.py`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `.githooks/pre-push`, docs, tests). The `llm` repo's v4 hook is
  a follow-up in that repo; `ContextHub` and others receive `pre-push.v2` (no suite gate) and need
  nothing.
- **No synthetic saturation.** Measurement must be read-only log analysis; the host is live and a
  synthetic burst would manufacture the very contention being measured (same deliberate scope
  decision as `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV`).
- **Cache correctness first.** Never degrade to a state-independent fallback key and never serve a
  tree verdict for a different tree; an unfingerprintable run simply executes fresh.
- **POSIX `sh` hook.** No new dependency, no `bash`-isms in `.githooks/pre-push`.
- **Test execution policy.** All test runs go through the test skill (`run_tests.py`); no ad-hoc
  `pytest` invocations.
- **Do not edit the pacer/lane semantics** delivered by `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV` — this item only
  measures them and changes cache keying.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test_cache.py` — tree-SHA helper usable from a committed (not just staged) state, plus the
  existing `fingerprint_kind` plumbing.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — CLI flag for an explicit tree fingerprint, threaded to
  `run_suite`/`run_all`/`run_cached`.
- `.githooks/pre-push` — add the pushed-commit guard, compute `HEAD^{tree}`, pass it, report hit/miss.
- `tests/test_test_cache.py` — same-tree hit / different-tree miss / fail-closed cases.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_commit_tree.py` — cross-consumer reuse assertion.
- `tests/unit/test-pre-push-hook.mjs` — hook-level assertions (flag presence, refusal paths).
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`, `docs/dev/git-hooks.md` — contract updates.
- Measurement: pi session logs under `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` plus existing tooling in
  `scripts/measure_audit_performance.py` as the pattern for a one-off analysis script.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — measurement window is thin.** ~13 h of post-fix logs with 12 samples today; if the
  window yields too few samples the criterion is "no regression observed in N samples", clearly
  labelled, with a re-check date. *Mitigation:* report sample counts alongside percentiles.
- **Risk — cache poisoning by a wrong tree key.** A bug here could serve a green verdict for an
  untested tree. *Mitigation:* fail closed, plus explicit same-tree/different-tree tests and reuse of
  the already-audited `fingerprint_kind` machinery.
- **Risk — hook divergence drift.** Per-repo copies (`llm` v4, `pre-push.v2`) mean the fix can land
  in `SorraAgents` yet not reach a project. *Mitigation:* AC6 + a follow-up item per diverged hook.
- **Risk — scope creep into the wider RCA amplifiers** (`drive` nested waits, finish lock
  serialisation, agents raising `TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` to 5400 s). Recorded as linked follow-ups, not
  scope.
- **Assumption —** the dominant residual cost is the dev-push gate suite, not finish, because finish
  no longer runs a full suite (`SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`). The AC1 measurement either confirms or
  refutes this, and refutation re-opens the amplifier list rather than silently narrowing the item.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV` — fast lane + calibrated ceiling + `slot_wait` reporting (**shipped
  `a2659c38`**); supersedes AC1–AC3 of the original RCA.
- `LP-0MVWZ8QPY000UVQM` (llm) — the original RCA item; closed as superseded, its AC4 residual and
  AC5 re-measurement are this item's scope.
- `SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81` — full-suite testing deferred to the dev-push gate (makes AC4 of the old
  item largely obsolete and creates the reuse gap addressed here).
- `SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB` / `SA-0MVQHVKUH009VQMD` — tree-bound finish verdicts and their documented
  contract (the precedent this item extends to the pre-push gate).
- `SA-0MVU8XRBQ000DG9D` — runner duration/timeout/kill/slot-wait facts (source of
  `slot_wait_seconds`).
- Open amplifiers, already tracked: `SA-0MVWKZ4QD006L2E0` (a low-ceiling waiter never probes
  higher-numbered free slots), `SA-0MVSJX5HS002JDHI` (dev pushes starve/flake under load),
  `SA-0MVEEALZR0029DD7` (single-flight coalescing of identical in-flight suite runs).
- `SA-0MVTET8KQ0031R6Z` — finish gate: classify timeouts/kills and report slot queue wait separately.
- Pushed-commit-guard precedents: `LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9` (llm v4 hook guard),
  `LP-0MVTI2K2A002HCGT` (llm: gate validated the main checkout, not the pushed commit — completed).
- Adjacent, open, *not* in scope: `SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3` / `SA-0MVU0IS9S006BFE3` (implement.py must
  push from the tree it is pushing) and `SA-0MVV1V1DB0035Q6B` (gate did not execute for the pushed
  commit) — they concern which tree `finish` pushes, not the hook's own fingerprint.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (producer, interactive reply):** "`SA-0MVWZQ269009SJXV` already holds AC1–AC3; what should
  happen to `LP-0MVWZ8QPY000UVQM`?" — Options: (a) close as superseded and file the residual here,
  (b) narrow the `llm` item and implement cross-repo, (c) close as fully superseded and drop
  AC4/AC5.
  **Answer: "1. A"** — close the `llm` item as superseded; the residual (AC4 gap + AC5
  re-measurement) is filed as this item. Source: interactive reply, this session. Research:
  verified `a2659c38` in `SorraAgents` (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY_DEFAULT == 6`, `test-fast` lane,
  live `slot_lane=fast`, `slot_wait=0.00007s`); verified none of the named files exist in the `llm`
  checkout, so an `llm`-store item could not satisfy worktree isolation.
- **Q2 (producer, interactive reply):** "Residual scope?" — Options: (a) re-measure only,
  (b) re-measure + tree-keyed pre-push gate, (c) re-measure + the wider amplifiers from the RCA.
  **Answer: "2. b"**; producer also asked for follow-up work to be recommended and offered as new
  work items rather than silently folded in. Source: interactive reply, this session. Research:
  `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` § "Explicit-fingerprint override" documents that the pre-push
  gate keys on loose worktree state; `run_cached`/`run_suite` already accept an explicit tree
  fingerprint, so the change is a CLI + hook plumbing problem, not a cache redesign.
- **Q3 (agent, resolved by inspection, no producer input needed):** "Does `implement finish` still run
  a full suite whose verdict the pre-push gate could reuse?" — **Answer: no**; finish defers the
  full suite to the dev-push gate (`SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81`, `fe85415a`, 2026-10-19), which is why the
  old AC4 is re-scoped to cross-consumer keying rather than finish→pre-push handoff. Source:
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` step 3b comment.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVWNHLQQ002TFZR** – GitHub closes the idle SSH connection during the pre-push full-suite gate, silently discarding a green gate (open)
- **SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG** – Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md after git pull (completed)
- **SA-0MQVIXRSE000AYCA** – Convert /plan command to a pi skill with bundled helpers (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mvecqugf0064u81, ac1, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+421 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mvecqugf0064u81, ac1, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+395 more)

## Goal

As a producer/agent, I want a single, reproducible per-test-file **keep / rework / prune** verdict that combines churn, mutation, anti-pattern and runtime evidence, so test-value decisions are made from one reconciled report rather than four separate reads.

## Problem statement

Today the evidence for test value is fragmented across `skill/test-churn` (evolution/growth), the mutation-testing campaign (`SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`, fault detection), `evaluate_usefulness.py` + `test-writing-guidelines.md` (static anti-patterns) and the test runner (runtime/flake). Each answers a different question; none produces an auditable per-file verdict. Epic `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` needs a repeatable classify → prove → report pipeline, and this skill is the missing connective tissue between those signals.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ingests, per test file: churn metrics (rewrite/growth/stability), mutation score, anti-pattern verdicts, and runtime/flake data when available.
- [ ] Emits one verdict per file — `keep`, `rework` or `prune` — with the evidence for that verdict recorded.
- [ ] Totals reconcile: verdict counts sum to files in scope, and every verdict cites at least one evidence source.
- [ ] Produces `test_value_report.md` + `test_value_data.json` with documented definitions and limitations.
- [ ] Orchestrates the existing analysers; it does not reimplement churn, mutation or anti-pattern detection.
- [ ] Missing inputs degrade honestly (the report states which signals were absent; it never fabricates a verdict).
- [ ] Reproducible (pinned inputs, documented command, deterministic ordering) and covered by tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Read-only against the analysed project.
- Must not turn a heuristic into an automatic deletion; `prune` is advisory and conservative.
- No per-project hardcoded paths; project root is an argument.
- Follows the repository skill contract and `$(skill_path ...)` shared-library resolution.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic (classify/prove/report).
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing on top-churn modules (behavioural evidence arm).
- `skill/test-churn`, `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`, `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.

Created from the intake discussion on `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`. Priority reflects that the aggregator is most useful once mutation evidence exists; it can be planned but should not land before the mutation-testing arm.

## Goal

As a test-value reviewer, I want a cheap static measure of how a test asserts and how much it relies on mocks, so I can pre-filter the suites that mutation testing should examine and give `toHaveBeenCalledWith`-style coupling an enforceable signal.

## Problem statement

`evaluate_usefulness.py` detects only crude anti-patterns (source-grep, placeholder, zero assertions, self-referential). It cannot distinguish a test that asserts observable behaviour from one that asserts internal collaborator calls, nor quantify mock density — yet mock density is a central independent variable in the hypothesis that high-volume mock-heavy suites detect fewer faults. Without this signal, the mutation campaign has no cheap way to choose where to spend its runtime.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parses TypeScript/JavaScript (and ideally Python) test files and reports per file: assertion count, assertions on internal collaborators vs public behaviour, mock/stub/spy count and ratio, and tests with no meaningful assertion.
- [ ] Flags `toHaveBeenCalledWith`/mock-call assertions on internal collaborators as a distinct, actionable signal (aligned with `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G`).
- [ ] Emits JSON + Markdown with documented definitions and conservative thresholds.
- [ ] Handles dynamic/indirect assertion styles without crashing, and reports uncertainty rather than a false verdict.
- [ ] Runs as a cheap pre-filter (no test execution) and documents that it is a proxy, not ground truth.
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Static analysis only; never executes the target project's tests.
- Conservative: uncertainty is reported, never auto-pruned.
- Language-neutral entry point with per-language adapters; no hardcoded project paths.

## Related work

- `SA-0MV28WX8Y005B05G` — prefer interface/behaviour assertions over `toHaveBeenCalledWith` on internal collaborators.
- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic.
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing (ground truth).
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`, `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`.

discovered-from:SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O

## Notes

Created from the intake discussion on `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O`. This is a pre-filter for the mutation campaign, not a replacement for it.

## Goal

As a maintainer of a large test suite, I want to detect near-duplicate test blocks and files, so additive accumulation can be measured and redundant coverage pruned with evidence.

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis measured large net test growth (+137,022 lines on the reference project) with a low rewrite ratio — the failure mode is additive accumulation, not churn. `evaluate_usefulness.py`'s "duplicate coverage" check is a heuristic and cannot find near-duplicates introduced through different import paths or copy-paste variation. Without clone detection, redundancy grows unnoticed because nothing forces a re-examination.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Detects near-duplicate test blocks (within and across files) using normalised AST/token similarity, not raw text matching.
- [ ] Reports clusters with file, line range and similarity score, ordered by redundancy.
- [ ] Distinguishes legitimate repetition (table-driven cases, parameterised variants) from redundant duplication, and defaults to reporting rather than removal.
- [ ] Emits JSON + Markdown with thresholds and limitations documented.
- [ ] Performance is bounded on a large suite (documented sampling/scope options).
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Read-only; no automatic deletion.
- Conservative thresholds; a false "duplicate" verdict is worse than a miss.
- No hardcoded project paths.

## Related work

- `SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO` — test-value refactor epic (additive accumulation is its stated failure mode).
- `SA-0MV28WY5Q003N54O` — mutation testing; this analyser is a complementary cheap signal.
- `skill/test-churn`, `skill/test/scripts/evaluate_usefulness.py`.

## Goal

As a producer, I want per-test runtime and flake history so I can express test value as fault detection per second of suite runtime and bound the cost of periodic mutation campaigns.

## Problem statement

Test value is currently measured without its cost. The test runner reports suite-level timing, but there is no per-test timing or flake history, so a valuable-but-slow test and a worthless-but-slow test are indistinguishable, and mutation-campaign runtime cannot be allocated sensibly. The test-value epic (`SA-0MVSGIMHK004QHOO`, AC7) also needs before/after runtime evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The test runner records per-test duration and a bounded flake history across runs.
- [ ] Emits a machine-readable report consumable by the test-value aggregator (churn/mutation/runtime join).
- [ ] Overhead is bounded and documented; normal runs stay within the existing runtime budget.
- [ ] Flake detection is deterministic for repeated failures and does not hide genuine failures.
- [ ] Integrated into the existing `skill/test` runner rather than a new measurement skill.
- [ ] Covered by tests; all related documentation updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Must not change the pass/fail semantics of the test runner.
- History storage is bounded (retention policy documented).
- Follows the test-execution policy: agents still invoke tests only via the test skill; infrastructure gates are out of scope.

# Intake Brief: Repeat producer actions in red on the final report conclusion

## Problem statement

The canonical end-of-session report (`skill/report`) lists blocking producer
actions in `## Producer Actions`, but the `## Conclusion` — the last thing the
operator reads — does not repeat them. When a session ends with something the
producer must do (answer a question, make a decision, grant an approval), the
operator can miss it in the body of a long report. Repeating any genuine
producer action in the Conclusion in red makes the blocking call-to-action
impossible to overlook.

## Users

- **Producer/operator** reading end-of-session reports in the pi TUI: wants the
  blocking action to stand out at the end of the report, not be buried mid-page.
- **Agent (intake/plan/implement/audit/…) authoring the report**: keeps passing
  blocking actions via `--producer-actions`; the renderer handles the red
  repetition deterministically (no per-skill change).

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when a skill session needs a decision from me, I want that
  decision repeated in red in the conclusion so I cannot miss it."
- "As a producer, when nothing is required of me, I do not want a red warning in
  the conclusion."
- "As an agent, I want the renderer to do this automatically so every skill
  behaves the same way."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the normalised producer actions are a genuine, non-`None needed`
   action, `render_report()` appends the action text **verbatim** to the
   `## Conclusion` section, wrapped in ANSI SGR red (`\x1b[31m…\x1b[0m`) with a
   `⚠️ Producer action required:` lead-in. Verified by unit test asserting the
   escape sequences and the exact action text inside `## Conclusion`.
2. When no producer actions are supplied, or the supplied text is routine
   workflow progression that normalises to `None needed`, the Conclusion
   contains no ANSI escape sequences and no repeated action text. Verified by
   unit tests (absent actions; `Proceed to /skill:plan`; `Review the brief, then
   run /skill:plan`).
3. Colour can be disabled with a new `--no-colour` CLI flag **or** the standard
   `NO_COLOR` environment variable (non-empty). In that mode the Conclusion
   still repeats the action in plain text with the `⚠️` marker and contains no
   ANSI escape sequences. Verified by unit tests for both opt-outs.
4. Multi-line / multi-action producer text is repeated verbatim (line breaks
   preserved) and the rest of the report is unchanged: section order,
   `## Producer Actions` → `## Notes` → `## Conclusion`, the existing
   completed/incomplete conclusion sentences, and the `</end_session>`
   terminator. Verified by regression tests.
5. `skill/report/SKILL.md` documents the conditional red repetition in the
   canonical template, the layout rules, and the colour opt-out
   (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`) alongside the existing icon opt-out. Verified
   by document review.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Implement in the shared renderer only (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`)
  plus a small shared colour helper — do not fork report logic into the ~17
  calling skills.
- Repeat **after** routine-next-step normalisation (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW): a
  routine next step must never produce red text.
- Do not use TTY detection to decide colour: the CLI's stdout is captured/piped
  by agents before being pasted into the final response, so TTY detection would
  disable the feature exactly where it is needed. Opt-out must be explicit
  (`--no-colour` / `NO_COLOR`).
- Colour is decorative: the `⚠️` marker and the plain action text must carry the
  meaning when colour is unavailable, so the report stays readable in
  non-ANSI consumers (GitHub, plain-text logs).
- No new runtime dependency; pure-Python, offline-testable.
- Do not change `## Producer Actions` semantics, the pane-status derivation, or
  the existing conclusion wording.

## Existing state

- `render_report()` renders `## Producer Actions` from the normalised
  `producer_actions` string (`None needed` when absent), then `## Notes`, then
  `## Conclusion`.
- The Conclusion currently emits one of two fixed sentences based on AC
  verdicts (`_derive_session_status`): completed → "This completes … Ready for
  `<next_action>`."; incomplete → "… is incomplete. Requires attention
  (`<next_action>`)." Nothing else is appended.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` already provides `icons_enabled(no_icons, env)`
  honouring `--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1` — the convention to mirror for
  colour, but colour must be a separate switch (`WL_NO_ICONS` must not disable
  colour).
- No ANSI/colour handling exists anywhere in the report renderer today (the
  only ANSI in the repo is in `tests/integration/test-worktree-workflow.sh`).

## Desired change

- Add `colour_enabled(no_colour=False, env=None)` (and `RED`/`RESET` constants)
  to `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`: enabled by default; disabled by
  `--no-colour` or a non-empty `NO_COLOR`.
- In `render_report()`, after the existing conclusion sentence(s), when the
  normalised producer actions are not `None needed`, append a blank line and a
  red line: `⚠️ Producer action required: <verbatim action text>`. Apply
  `RED … RESET` only when colour is enabled.
- Thread an optional `no_colour: bool = False` parameter through
  `render_report()`, `render_report_from_workitem()`, `render_from_wl()` and the
  CLI, adding the `--no-colour` flag.
- Update `skill/report/SKILL.md` (template, layout rules, example, colour
  opt-out) and the `README.md` report-helper bullet to mention the red
  repetition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — conditional red repetition in the
  Conclusion; `no_colour` plumbing and `--no-colour` flag.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` helper + `RED`/`RESET`
  constants mirroring `icons_enabled()`.
- `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` — new tests: red repetition,
  no-repetition for absent/routine actions, `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR` fallback,
  multi-line preservation, structure regression.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_herdr_pane.py` — `colour_enabled()` unit tests.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — template/layout/example + colour opt-out docs.
- `README.md` — report-helper bullet: note the red repetition of blocking
  producer actions in the Conclusion.

## Related work

- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** — "Don't include producer actions that are next steps"
  (completed): established normalisation to `None needed`; the red repetition
  must run after it.
- **SA-0MULPQ3BK001A1M5** — "Misleading completion message on LLM summaries"
  (completed): made the Conclusion reflect session status; this item extends the
  same section.
- **SA-0MTFLQEQQ0083EW1** — "Update pane title with status emoticon on skill
  completion" (completed): established the ✅/⚠️/🚫 status colour semantics this
  feature reuses for a red call-to-action.
- **SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S** — "Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting
  via helper report skill" (completed): origin of the canonical report contract.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "red font" means ANSI SGR red in terminal output.** The report
  is rendered to stdout and pasted into the pi TUI; ANSI is the only mechanism
  that reliably colours that path. If the producer expects Markdown/HTML
  colouring, the brief should be revised before implementation (documented in
  the Appendix).
- **Assumption — red repeats blocking actions only.** Because routine workflow
  progression is normalised to `None needed` first, it can never trigger red;
  this avoids the false "producer is blocking" signal fixed by
  SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW.
- **Assumption — no TTY detection.** Explicit opt-out only, because agent-captured
  stdout is not a TTY.
- **Risk — ANSI leakage into non-terminal consumers** (GitHub, PRs, plain logs).
  Mitigation: `--no-colour`/`NO_COLOR`, plus the `⚠️` marker and plain text so the
  meaning survives even if escapes are stripped or shown literally.
- **Risk — colour-blindness / theme contrast.** Mitigation: the `⚠️` marker and
  the words "Producer action required" carry the signal; colour is decorative.
- **Risk — multi-line producer text.** Mitigation: wrap the whole block once and
  test line-break preservation rather than prefixing each line.
- **Scope creep.** Adjacent ideas (colouring the `## Producer Actions` section,
  colourising AC verdicts, HTML-export colour) are out of scope — record as
  separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What does 'red font' mean for a Markdown report rendered by the LLM/TUI —
  ANSI escape codes, HTML `<span style=\"color:red\">`, or plain emphasis?"
  — **Answer (repo research + design analysis):** ANSI SGR red. The report is
  printed to stdout and pasted into the terminal-rendered TUI; raw ANSI passes
  through and colours the terminal, whereas inline HTML styles are not honoured
  by the Markdown→terminal path and GitHub strips `style` attributes. Recorded
  as an assumption; the producer can request an HTML/bold variant at review.
  No interactive round was required for the rest of the brief.
- Q: "Should routine next-step actions (e.g. 'Proceed to /skill:plan') also be
  repeated in red?" — **Answer (SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW contract):** No. Routine
  workflow progression is normalised to `None needed` and must never be shown as
  a blocking red action; only genuine, current-stage actions are repeated.
- Q: "Should colour be auto-detected (TTY) or explicitly opt-out?" — **Answer
  (design analysis):** Explicit opt-out only. Agent-captured stdout is not a
  TTY, so TTY detection would silently disable the feature on the exact path
  that needs it. `--no-colour` and `NO_COLOR` are the opt-outs.

### Related work items
- **SA-0MVQ1QM9L0083KAW** – Producer Actions contract: docs and skill templates (completed)
- **SA-0MVNQ3RLW006XEFW** – Don't include producer actions that are next steps (completed)

## Observed

During an epic `implement.py drive` run, the first driven child (**SA-0MVTHIZE0007EAKZ**) was demoted from `in-progress` back to `open` by the herdr hydrator **four minutes into its implementation session**. The hydrator log:

```
2026-11-01T13:47:39.108Z [hydrator] released SA-0MVTHIZE0007EAKZ: in-progress/intake_complete → open/intake_complete (no pane, claim holder dead)
```

and the item comment it wrote:

```
herdr-hydrator: released because no pane and claim holder dead; previous assignee: (none)
```

The child session was alive and working (it had already written its red test).

## Root cause (evidence)

The hydrator's `kept … live claim holder` rule (WL-0MVWDB3IG004NRIU) is *the* protection for pane-less driven sessions: it probes `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock` for a live `flock`. But the lock is acquired inside the short-lived `implement.py start` **subprocess** and released when that process exits, so nothing holds the flock while the driven child session works. Measured while the session was alive:

```
$ cat .worklog/locks/child-SA-0MVTHIZE0007EAKZ.lock
{"agent":"implement","pid":396636,…}      # pid 396636 already dead
$ fuser -v .worklog/locks/child-SA-0MVTHIZE0007EAKZ.lock   # no holders
```

The spawned session's environment carries `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` and `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH`, but **no** `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN`, so the holder chain is broken at the `parent` → `start` → session boundary (the token is only propagated when the spawning process itself holds the lock, which `parent` does not).

## Impact

- A working driven child is reported `open` for the whole implementation: violates "actively worked ⇒ in_progress" and makes the herdr UI lie.
- `open` + a free lock makes the item **dispatchable again**: a second session can be spawned onto the same worktree (a second `phase_start` resumes it), i.e. two agents editing one tree.
- Every `drive`/`parent` run is exposed, since driven children are pane-less by construction.

## Desired fix (direction)

Make the driven session the lock holder for its own lifetime so the hydrator's live-claim-holder rule works as documented: either hold the `flock` in the long-lived driver for the child's duration **and** propagate the ownership token to the spawned session, or have the driven session acquire/hold the lock itself (re-entrant by token). The lock-file `pid` must name a live process, and `_probe_child_lock` must stay token-based (never pid-based).

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- [ ] While a driven child session is alive, `<worklog>/locks/child-<id>.lock` is held by a live `flock` and the hydrator keeps the item `in-progress`.
- [ ] The spawned session receives `IMPLEMENT_CHILD_LOCK_TOKEN` and its own `start`/`finish` re-enter instead of being refused (`skipped-held`).
- [ ] A test drives `phase_drive` with a fake spawner and asserts the lock is held for the session's lifetime and released after it exits.
- [ ] No regression in the existing per-child-lock tests.
data.title: Driven child sessions do not hold the per-child lock, so the herdr hydrator demotes them mid-implementation

discovered-from:SA-0MVTE927L0017ND5

## Observed

A driven child's `implement.py finish` gate hung for **33 minutes** on one test and was killed by the per-command timeout (2700 s). The pytest process was asleep, not computing (`wchan=hrtimer_nanosleep`, 4 s CPU in 32 min), and its open fds showed which test it was in:

```
lr-x------ 11 -> /tmp/pytest-of-rgardler/pytest-0/test_finish_refuses_when_lock_0/main/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock
lr-x------ 12 -> /tmp/pytest-of-rgardler/pytest-0/test_finish_refuses_when_lock_0/main/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock
```

The test is `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py::test_finish_refuses_when_lock_held_by_other_finish`, whose contract is *"a finish against a locked checkout exits non-zero"* — i.e. it must fail fast.

## Root cause

The harness does not neutralise the ambient lock-wait variables, so `phase_finish` honours whatever the caller exported:

- the drive was launched with `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT=10800` (needed because a real `finish` must wait for another session's long-held main-checkout lock),
- the test inherits that value and therefore **waits 3 hours** instead of refusing immediately, and
- the gate kills it at `timeoutPerCommand` and reports `reason: timeout` — a red gate whose cause is the test environment, not the change under test.

Any agent (or CI job) that exports `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` / `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` to make its own `finish` wait turns this test from milliseconds into a multi-hour hang. The same shape applies to every other test that exercises the lock-wait path.

## Impact

- A green change can be reported as a `timeout` gate failure purely because of the caller's environment.
- Long waits poison the whole group run: the run must be repeated with a different environment.
- The symptom is misleading (a hanging test with almost no CPU) and hard to attribute without inspecting `/proc/<pid>/fd`.

## Desired fix (direction)

Make the affected tests environment-hermetic, e.g. an autouse fixture (or the `_finish_harness`) that pins `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`/`IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` to `0` via `monkeypatch.setenv`/`delenv` for the duration of the test, and a comment saying why (the wait value is a caller policy, never a test input). Audit every test that reaches the lock-wait path the same way, and add a guard that fails if a test reads a wait timeout inherited from the ambient environment.

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- [ ] `pytest skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` passes in under a few seconds with `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT=10800` and `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT=600` exported.
- [ ] A regression test asserts the refusal path is reached without sleeping (e.g. patches the clock/wait and asserts it was never entered, or asserts elapsed < N seconds).
- [ ] The same hermeticity is applied to any other test that exercises `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` / `IMPLEMENT_START_LOCK_TIMEOUT` / test-slot waits.

## Goal

`_git_commit_evidence` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` resolves a
stranded child's pushed-commit evidence with
`git log <ref> --grep <child_id> -n 1`. `--grep` matches the **whole commit
message including the body**, so a commit that merely *mentions* a work-item id
counts as that item's work.

Observed 2026-11-01 during the epic drive for SA-0MVX1M6HH004YPX2: driven child
SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 timed out after 3600 s with its own commit (`9119e4117`)
still unpushed in its worktree, and `drive` reported it as *stranded* with
evidence `0fb0e4305` — the **sibling** child's (SA-0MVX31GLC002IPR8) commit,
whose body names SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 as the future home of the detection
module. The verdict told the operator to `--finalise-stranded` a child whose
work had never been pushed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Commit evidence matches only commits whose **subject** references the
   work-item id, never a body-only mention.
2. A regression test pins the false-positive: a commit whose body mentions
   another item's id is not evidence for that item.
3. A driven child whose commit is still only in its own worktree is reported
   as non-terminal-with-work, not as stranded on the parent branch.

# audit skill: AC extraction rejects qualified `Acceptance Criteria` headings

**Symptom (observed auditing RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L, 2026-11-01):** `audit_runner.py issue` returned `Ready to close: No` with `No acceptance criteria defined.` and **0 model calls**, then demoted the item to `open`/`plan_complete` — even though the item's description carries three numbered acceptance criteria under the heading `## Acceptance criteria for this project`.

## Root cause

`_extract_acs()` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` matches the AC heading with an anchored regex:

```
^(?:Acceptance|Success)\s+Criteria:?\s*(?:\([^)]*\))?\s*$
```

The match is applied to the line **after** `_normalize_heading_line()` strips markdown heading markers — but a trailing qualifier such as `for this project` is not allowed (only an optional colon or parenthetical is), so the heading never matches and the function returns the `["No acceptance criteria defined."]` sentinel. The pipeline then treats that sentinel as the AC body (a `warning` verdict), skips Phase 2, and produces a `No` verdict which demotes the item.

## Consequences

- A valid, auditable item audits as if it has no ACs: Phase 1 and Phase 2 screening are skipped (0 pi calls), and the item is demoted to `open`/`plan_complete` on the normal `No` path.
- The failure is silent to the model — no prompt ever sees the AC list, so no evidence names the extraction failure.

## Reproduction

`audit_runner.py issue` against an item whose description AC-section heading carries a trailing qualifier, e.g. `## Acceptance criteria for this project` (RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L exhibited this; its three criteria were manually verified satisfied, and the heading had to be normalised to `## Acceptance Criteria` before the audit would screen them).

## Suggested fix

Relax the heading pattern to accept trailing free text while keeping canonical headings byte-compatible: e.g. match `Acceptance Criteria` / `Success Criteria` optionally followed by `:`, a parenthetical, a trailing qualifier (`for …`), or end-of-line. Add regression tests covering heading variants: canonical, lowercase `c`, colon, parenthetical, and a trailing-qualifier heading.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `_extract_acs()` (or the heading matcher it uses) recognises AC headings with a trailing qualifier (e.g. `## Acceptance criteria for this project`), extracting the numbered/bulleted items below them.
2. Canonical headings (`## Acceptance Criteria`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Success Criteria`, optional colon/parenthetical) behave unchanged — no regression.
3. A unit test covers the exact qualifier variant from the RISE-0MVXXKJGK004WO6L reproduction.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_extract_acs`, `_normalize_heading_line`)

---
