# Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs: transient SSH auth failures and push races make leaf `finish` fail after the work has landed

## Problem statement

On 2026-11-04 a single leaf session implementing two items (`WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R`,
`WL-0MW1VITA8009RLHQ` in ContextHub) spent far more time fighting git than
writing code. Five independent failures compounded, and the worst of them leaves
an item that **cannot be completed through the workflow at all**.

| # | Symptom | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Transient SSH auth failure is not classified as retryable → hard failure | blocking |
| 2 | Non-fast-forward is detected but a leaf session gets no automatic rebase-and-retry | blocking |
| 3 | `finish` cannot converge when the commit **already** landed on `origin/dev` | blocking |
| 4 | The push gate re-runs the full canonical suite on every retry attempt | cost |
| 5 | A full-suite gate failure under concurrent load is indistinguishable from a real regression at the point of failure | diagnosis |

### Evidence

**1. Flaky SSH auth (~1 in 3 attempts).** Measured directly, seconds apart, from
the same shell with no credential change:

```
try1: 75f64a61...  refs/heads/dev     (OK)
try2: git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey).
try3: 75f64a61...  refs/heads/dev     (OK)
```

`ssh -T git@github.com` also alternated between authenticated and
`Permission denied (publickey)`. There is no `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` in these sessions
(they run over SSH with an on-disk `id_ed25519`), so each connection is a fresh
key handshake — which is where the flakiness lives. Separately GitHub returned a
non-auth transport error once:

```
! [remote rejected]   HEAD -> dev (Internal Server Error)
```

`_push_to_dev` (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`) classifies only
non-fast-forward (`non-fast-forward` / `fetch first` / `remote contains work`).
Everything else — including `Permission denied (publickey)` and
`Could not read from remote repository` — falls through to
`LOG.error(...); return False`, i.e. an unconditional hard failure with a
misleading "Commit is local and can be pushed manually" hint.

**2. No rebase-and-retry for a leaf session.** `PushNonFastForwardError` carries a
`rebase_cmd` for the caller, and `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` includes
`("local_dev_fast_forward", ...)` / `("main_checkout_lock", "lock_held")` — but
that retry budget is applied by `phase_drive` to **driven children**. A plain
leaf `finish` invocation fails outright. Observed: `origin/dev` advanced **three
times** during one item's lifecycle (concurrent runs pushed
`WL-0MW109HU60042BVW`, `WL-0MW109IIN009PADE`), and every one of those required an
operator-side fetch/rebase/push loop.

**3. `finish` cannot converge once the commit has landed.** For
`WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R` the push eventually succeeded, and
`git merge-base --is-ancestor 58834b09 origin/dev` confirmed it was on the remote
(and `git log origin/dev` showed it). Re-running `finish` to complete the
lifecycle then *failed again* — it re-attempts the push, hits the flaky auth, and
on failure resets the item to `status=open` with `assignee` cleared:

```
INFO: Restored status=open for WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R (failure exit, assignee cleared)
WARNING: Push failed. Commit 58834b09 on branch ... is local and can be pushed manually.
```

The workflow therefore had no path to `in_review`; the lifecycle had to be
completed by hand with `wl update --status completed --stage in_review`, after
independently verifying ancestry. That manual step is the automation failing
open, not a design.

**4. Full-suite suite re-run per attempt.** Every push attempt runs the
pre-push gate (`push gate: running the full canonical suite (--scope full
--strict-git-env)`, ~180–260 s). Eight failed attempts ≈ 30+ minutes of pure
gate overhead. With `--no-cache` runs for diagnosis on top, the same tree was
fully tested at least four times in one session.

**5. Load-induced gate flake reads as a code failure.** One push attempt ended:

```
ERROR: Full test suite failed - the push to dev/main is blocked.
```

Re-running the identical tree: `327 passed | 1 skipped; 4580 passed | 5 skipped`
— green. The failures were seven unrelated files failing to *load*
(`Cannot find package '@worklog/shared/worklog-paths'`, i.e. a missing shared
build) under heavy concurrent load from sibling agent runs. Nothing in the
operator-facing failure said "load/environment", so the honest reading was "my
change broke the suite".

## Goal

A leaf `finish` run in a busy multi-agent checkout completes the item through
the normal lifecycle when its work is valid, treating transient git transport
and ref-race failures as recoverable, and never leaves an item stranded in
`open` while its commit sits on `origin/dev`.

User stories:

- "As an agent running `finish` on a repo where several sessions push in the same
  minute, I want a transient transport or non-fast-forward failure retried
  automatically, so a ref race does not cost me the work item's lifecycle."
- "As an operator, I want `finish` to tell me plainly whether the push failed or
  whether the push landed and a *verification* step failed, so I know whether to
  retry, rebase, or investigate."
- "As an agent whose push already landed, I want re-running `finish` to reach
  `in_review` without re-pushing, so the workflow can always be completed."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Transient transport failures are classified and retried.** Auth/transport
   signatures (`Permission denied (publickey)`, `Could not read from remote
   repository`, `Connection reset`/`timed out`, `Internal Server Error` on the
   remote side) are classified as **infrastructure**, distinct from a real
   content rejection. Retried on a bounded budget with backoff (reusing the
   existing `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT` semantics), and surfaced as such in the
   report — never as a bare "push failed".
2. **Non-fast-forward is retried for leaf runs, not only driven children.**
   `finish` rebases onto `origin/dev` and re-attempts within the same bounded
   budget. A rebase conflict is a genuine stop with an actionable message (never
   forced/mutated silently).
3. **`finish` converges when the commit already landed.** If `HEAD` is an
   ancestor of `origin/dev` (verified against the remote, not a stale
   remote-tracking ref), `finish` treats the push as satisfied, skips the
   re-push, and proceeds to the terminal `completed`/`in_review` transition
   instead of resetting the item to `open`.
4. **Push-failed and verification-failed are distinguishable** in both the log
   and the work-item comment: `push_failed` (nothing landed) vs
   `push_landed_but_unverified` (pushed, ancestry/gate assertion failed) vs
   `already_pushed`.
5. **No status regression on an already-landed push.** An item whose commit is on
   `origin/dev` is never returned to `open` by a transport failure.
6. **Reduced gate cost per attempt.** At most one full-suite gate run per
   `finish` invocation even across internal retries (the gate result for an
   unchanged tree is reused, or the retry path is reachable only *after* a
   successful gate), so N transport retries do not mean N full suites.
7. **A load/environment gate failure is labelled as such.** When the gate fails
   with suite *load* errors and a retry passes on the identical tree, the report
   says "infrastructure/load flake (suite failed to load on attempt N, passed
   unmodified on attempt N+1)" rather than reporting a code failure. This must
   not weaken the gate: a reproducible failure still blocks the push.
8. **Regression tests** drive a fake remote/git shim through: transient auth
   failure then success; non-fast-forward then successful rebase; ref race where
   the commit already landed; rebase conflict stop; and the labelled load-flake
   case.
9. **Documentation** (`skill/implement/SKILL.md` "When `finish` refuses" and the
   dev-push gate section) reflects the retry taxonomy and the three push
   outcomes.
10. **Full project test suite passes** (`/skill:test`).

## Plan

1. Extract push-outcome classification (transient vs content vs already-landed)
   from `_push_to_dev` into a pure, testable helper; unit-test the signature
   table. → verify: new test file green, table-driven over the five observed
   messages.
2. Add the bounded infrastructure retry + rebase-and-retry to the leaf `finish`
   path (reuse `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS`/`DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT` rather than a
   second mechanism). → verify: shim-driven tests for each recovery path.
3. Add the already-landed short-circuit (remote-verified ancestry) before the
   push, and guarantee no `open` regression in that case. → verify: test that a
   finish over an already-pushed commit reaches `in_review` with zero push
   attempts.
4. De-duplicate gate execution across internal retries. → verify: assertion on
   the shim's invocation count.
5. Label load-flake gate failures; keep reproducible failures blocking.
   → verify: paired tests (same tree fails-then-passes = flake label; fails
   twice = blocked).
6. Update `SKILL.md` and record the taxonomy. → verify: docs review, then
   `/skill:test` full.

## Key files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_push_to_dev`, `PushNonFastForwardError`,
  `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS`, `phase_finish`, the main-checkout lock guard, the
  termination/finish report.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — "When `finish` refuses", dev-push gate.
- Tests: the implement skill's existing python suites (fake-remote/shim fixtures).

## Risks & notes

- **Do not weaken the gate.** Retrying a *content* rejection or a reproducible
  suite failure must remain a hard stop. Only classified-transient conditions
  and labelled load flakes are retried, and a retry must re-verify the tree.
- **Never force-push.** Rebase-and-retry only; a conflict stops with an
  actionable message.
- **Remote-verified ancestry** is mandatory for the already-landed short-circuit:
  a stale `origin/dev` remote-tracking ref would otherwise let an unpushed commit
  be treated as landed. Fetch (or `ls-remote`) before asserting.
- **`main-checkout.lock` is working as designed** and is out of scope: it
  correctly fail-closed when a concurrent run held it, and a leaf session
  waiting on a live holder is safer than racing it. The gap is only that a leaf
  run has no bounded wait — consider that separately (the drive path already has
  `_wait_for_main_checkout_lock`).
- **Environment note (not a repo defect):** these sessions run over SSH with no
  `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, so every connection is a fresh key handshake. A per-session
  ssh-agent or `ControlMaster` would remove the transport flake at the source;
  that is an operator-environment remedy, and the work item's ACs deliberately do
  not depend on it being adopted.
- **Observability.** Record the retry taxonomy and the three push outcomes on the
  work item comment, so a post-hoc reader can tell a transport flake from a real
  rejection without re-running anything.

## Related

- Discovered during the 2026-11-04 overnight zero-dispatch RCA follow-up, while
  implementing `WL-0MW1VINII003IL7R` (commit `58834b09`) and
  `WL-0MW1VITA8009RLHQ` (commit `f5566e2d`) in ContextHub.
- ContextHub `WL-0MVHP5S01006GDDV` — repo pre-push hook does not run the test
  suite (canonical gate unenforced at push): the counterpart that made the gate
  mandatory, and therefore made these retry costs visible.
- The `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` / `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT` machinery
  (LP-0MVWEP292000ODBS) is the existing precedent this item extends to leaf runs.
- `WL-0MW109HU60042BVW`, `WL-0MW109IIN009PADE` — the concurrent ContextHub runs
  whose pushes advanced `origin/dev` mid-flight.
data.title: Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs: transient SSH auth failures and push races make leaf finish fail after the work has landed

# Harden /tmp inode headroom — age-based cleanup for test churn directories (host runbook)

## Goal (user story)

As the host owner of a multi-agent workstation, I want age-based cleanup of the
directories that test and build runs churn in `/tmp`, so inode headroom is
reclaimed automatically and a future runner that skips the framework prune
still cannot exhaust `/tmp` inodes.

## Context

Follow-up to the critical framework item (disk-backed `TMPDIR` + stale
pytest-root prune in `run_tests.py`/`implement.py`). That fix prevents new
inode pressure from the test runner; this item is the **host-level belt-and-
braces**: `systemd-tmpfiles` currently only carries `q /tmp 1777 root root 10d`,
so rapid multi-agent churn (stale `pytest-of-*` roots, Playwright/Chromium
profiles, `tsx`/node compile caches) can still fill the tmpfs inode table long
before the 10-day sweep. Observed in practice: `/tmp` at 100 % inodes
(1,048,576 total) while byte usage was ~24 %.

## Desired change (option 3)

Add age-based cleanup rules (systemd-tmpfiles preferred; cron acceptable where
tmpfiles is unavailable) for the high-churn temp directories, with an age
threshold longer than the longest test run, and document a runbook so the
remediation is repeatable.

Candidate patterns (refine during implementation):

- `/tmp/pytest-of-%u/pytest-*`
- `/tmp/playwright*`, `/tmp/.org.chromium.Chromium.*`, `/tmp/.com.google.Chrome.*`
- `/tmp/tsx-*`, `/tmp/node-compile-cache*`

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Rules installed and version-controlled/documented.** Age-based cleanup
   rules exist for the churn patterns above (e.g. `/etc/tmpfiles.d/pi-test-tmp.conf`
   with `e`/`q` lines, age ≥ 1 day), with the exact content recorded in the
   repo (runbook or a committed template under `docs/dev/` or `scripts/`).
2. **Verified.** `systemd-tmpfiles --clean --dry-run` (or the cron equivalent)
   lists the intended removals, and a before/after `df -i /tmp` demonstrates
   reclaimed inodes. Evidence captured in a work-item comment.
3. **Safety.** The age threshold is strictly greater than the longest full-suite
   run (currently ~48 min measured worst case), rules are user-scoped where
   possible, and the active `pytest-current` target / newest root is never
   removed.
4. **Runbook.** `docs/dev/testing.md` (or a new `docs/dev/host-hygiene.md`)
   documents install, verify, rollback, and the inode-exhaustion failure
   signature (`ENOSPC` in Playwright `createContext`, `df -i /tmp` at 100 %,
   gate `reason: unparsed`/`infrastructure`).
5. **No repo code change required for the cleanup itself** beyond the committed
   rule template/runbook; if a scripted installer is added, it is idempotent
   and requires explicit root/host opt-in.

## Key files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/testing.md` or `docs/dev/host-hygiene.md` — runbook + rule template.
- Optional: a committed `scripts/` template for `/etc/tmpfiles.d/` (documented,
  not auto-installed without opt-in).

## Constraints

- **Requires host/root access** (`/etc/tmpfiles.d/`, `systemd-tmpfiles`). The
  repository change is documentation/template only; the host change is applied
  by the operator and evidenced in a work-item comment.
- Do **not** add rules that delete recent or active test roots.
- Complements, and does not replace, the framework TMPDIR + prune item.

## Related work

- Critical framework fix (option 1 + 2): disk-backed `TMPDIR` + stale
  pytest-root prune in `run_tests.py`/`implement.py`.
- Observed during **MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV** (tce-main-street) dev-push gate.

## Risks

- Over-aggressive age thresholds can delete a long-running test's temp files —
  mitigate with a threshold well above the measured worst case and user scoping.
- Host config drift between machines — the committed rule template keeps it
  reproducible.
data.title: Harden /tmp inode headroom — age-based cleanup for test churn directories (host runbook)

# finish: retry the local-dev fast-forward after the recovery rebase, and report a pushed-commit-guard refusal distinctly

## Goal (user story)

As an agent whose `dev` push follows a concurrent `dev` advance, when `implement.py finish`
cannot fast-forward the main checkout before the push, I want finish to still leave the main
checkout's `dev` at the pushed commit after the recovery rebase, and to report a
pushed-commit-guard refusal distinguishably (pushed sha, gate HEAD, gate tree) naming the
worktree push as recovery — instead of a generic push failure.

## Background

Cross-reference: **LP-0MVWB6AOH001MAB0** (llm worklog) — "finish pushes from the main checkout
after a refused local-dev fast-forward, so the pre-push pushed-commit guard refuses". The
producer decided (2026-11-05) that the residual scope lands here (SorraAgents) and the llm item
is kept as a cross-reference that owns no code.

The core symptom (push from the main checkout) was already fixed by **SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3**:
`phase_finish` Step 6 and `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` now push from the worktree that holds
the commit. The residual gaps are:

- **AC1 (fast-forward retry).** `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` is called only once, in Step 5,
  *before* the push. When it is refused with `local_dev_diverged` / `commit_not_based_on_remote_tip`
  because a sibling moved `dev`, the recovery rebase produces a commit that *is* based on
  `origin/dev`, but the fast-forward is never retried, so the main checkout's local `dev` stays
  behind the pushed commit.
- **AC4 (distinguishable guard refusal).** When `.githooks/pre-push` §3a refuses a push because
  the gate tree is not the pushed commit (or is dirty at it), `git_push_to_dev` finds no
  `gate_reason=` line and reports a generic push failure. Finish cannot tell the operator that
  the guard refused, nor surface the pushed sha / gate HEAD / gate tree the guard printed.

## Scope

In scope: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (the fast-forward retry inside the non-fast-forward
recovery, and a distinct pushed-commit-guard-refusal classification) and its regression tests.

Out of scope: changing `.githooks/pre-push` in consuming projects. The guard's existing stable
diagnostic text is the contract this item detects against; a hook-side `gate_reason=` emission is
a separate follow-up owned by the llm item.

## Acceptance criteria

1. After a **refused** local-dev fast-forward (`local_dev_diverged` / `commit_not_based_on_remote_tip`),
   when `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` rebases the feature branch onto `origin/dev`, `finish`
   **retries** the fast-forward for the rebased commit and records the retry in
   `report["steps"]["local_dev_fast_forward"]`. When the retry succeeds, the main checkout's
   checked-out `dev` HEAD equals the pushed commit before the retry push.
2. The retried fast-forward never fails the finish: a second refusal is recorded (with its
   reason) and the push still proceeds from the worktree — the current recovery behaviour is
   preserved.
3. `finish` detects the pre-push pushed-commit guard's refusal from its stable diagnostic text and
   reports it distinguishably as `report["steps"]["push"]["reason"] == "refused_by_pushed_commit_guard"`
   carrying the **pushed sha**, the **gate HEAD** and the **gate tree** parsed from the guard's
   output, with recovery guidance that names the worktree push. A non-guard push failure keeps its
   existing classification (`test_failure`, `timeout`, `subject_mismatch`, …).
4. Regression tests drive the **concurrent-move shape** (worktree based on `dev~1`, another commit
   landed on `origin/dev`) and assert the guard's preconditions hold at push time: pushed sha ==
   gate-tree HEAD and the gate tree is clean; and assert the main checkout's `dev` is advanced to
   the pushed commit after the recovery rebase. A second test asserts a guard-refusal stderr is
   classified `refused_by_pushed_commit_guard` with the three values, and a generic failure is not.
5. Full project test suite passes.

## Notes

- Guard: `.githooks/pre-push` §3a (LP-0MVSJUM3O003C0H9); its refusal prints
  `ERROR: pre-push gate refuses this push: the tree it would measure is not the pushed commit.`
  followed by `pushed commit  (refs/heads/dev): <sha>`, `checked-out HEAD: <sha>`,
  `gate tree: <path>` (and a dirty-tree variant).
- `git_push_to_dev` is around line 4815; `_recover_non_fast_forward_push` around line 10021;
  `_fast_forward_local_dev_for_push` around line 6783.
- Related completed: SA-0MVTFMB7K002Y1F3 (push from worktree), SA-0MVSJX5HS002DJHI (gate reason
  vocabulary / transport retry).

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:_resolve_merge_base()` returns the **candidate ref name** (`origin/dev`) rather than the SHA resolved by `git merge-base`, and `compute_changed_files()` then runs `git diff --name-only <ref>` against that name.

When an implement worktree's branch base is *behind* the ref (a stale base — e.g. the branch was forked while local `dev` lagged `origin/dev`), diffing against the ref includes **dev-side** commits that are not part of the change set. `select_group_from_changed_files()` then picks test groups for unrelated work.

Discovered-from: WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ (ContextHub store) — the stale-base session in which this was observed.

## Evidence

- Observed on 2026-11-05 in a ContextHub implement session (WL-0MW3JIYIR002RCP8): a docs + `tests/setup-tests.ts` change set ran `npm test -- packages/herdr/src` because the stale base made the diff include dev-side `packages/herdr` commits.
- Current code (`run_tests.py`, `_resolve_merge_base`, ~line 506): the loop runs `git merge-base <candidate> HEAD`, then `return candidate` (the ref name) — the resolved `proc.stdout.strip()` SHA is discarded.
- `compute_changed_files()` (~line 462) passes the returned value straight into `git diff --name-only <base>`.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `implement.py finish` / `run_tests.py --scope changed` — depend on correct changed-file selection.
- **Operators / CI** — depend on changed-scope runs exercising the code that actually changed.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, when my worktree forked from a base behind `origin/dev`, I want changed-scope selection to measure only *my* diff, so the gate runs the right tests.
- As an operator, I want a stale base to degrade into a smaller diff, never into an unrelated named group.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_resolve_merge_base()` returns the SHA resolved by `git merge-base` (falling back to the next candidate only when `merge-base` yields nothing), never a bare ref name.
- [ ] `compute_changed_files()` diffs against a merge-base SHA, so commits that exist on the ref but not on the branch base are excluded from the change set.
- [ ] Regression test: a fixture repo whose branch base is one commit behind the target ref — the changed-file set must contain only the branch's own files, not the ref-side files.
- [ ] Fallback behaviour preserved: with no usable base the function still returns `None` and callers fall back to full scope (no crash).
- [ ] Documentation updated where the changed-scope base semantics are described (`skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`) if the returned value's contract changes.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Probe/read-only of git state; no new runtime dependencies; reuse existing helpers (`_git_inspection_env`, `run_cmd`).
- Behaviour change must be conservative: an unresolved base must still fall back to full scope rather than an empty diff.
- Related but distinct from SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66 (unqualified `origin/dev` ref *ambiguity* with a shadowing local branch) — both live in the same function, so either item may be implemented first; if both are taken together, keep the two fixes as separate commits.
- All written output in UK English.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_resolve_merge_base()` must return the merge-base SHA; `compute_changed_files()` consumes it unchanged.
- `skill/test/tests/` (or the existing test-skill test location) — regression test for a stale-base fixture.
- `skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — document the returned-value contract if it is described there.

## Related work

- ContextHub `WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ` — Main-checkout local dev diverged from origin/dev (the stale-base incident; records this hand-off).
- `SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66` — Stale local branch named origin/dev makes origin/dev ambiguous (adjacent defect in the same function).
data.title: run_tests.py _resolve_merge_base returns the ref name instead of the merge-base SHA — changed scope picks up ref-side commits

Discovered while implementing SA-0MW3FF18I003KGZE children 1-2 (2026-11-05).

The repository's finish gate and dev-push full-suite runs repeatedly hit the 2700 s per-command timeout under nominal multi-agent host load (full suite observed taking 15-45+ min depending on concurrent suites; verified green runs exist in .worklog/cache). The gate diagnostics classify these as reason=timeout - infrastructure, not code failures - and the documented remedy is to raise timeoutPerCommand in .pi/test-config.json with headroom over a green run's elapsed time.

ACs:
- .pi/test-config.json sets a timeoutPerCommand with headroom over the slowest observed green full-suite run under load (e.g. 5400 s), with the change committed and pushed via a work item.
- A re-run of a previously-timed-out gate for an unchanged tree completes green.

Not urgent (gates converge via cache retry), out of scope for the tracking epic.

data.description:
## Headline

Make the audit skill immune to a dirty/stale main checkout by running its
execution-dependent work (full-suite green-run gate, and ideally the whole
Phase 1/2 pipeline) inside a **fresh detached worktree checked out at the
latest `origin/dev`** (or the item's merged tip), so an un-pushed in-flight
commit sitting on the main `dev` branch can never contaminate an audit.

## Problem statement

`audit_runner.py` resolves ALL git-derived audit content (HEAD sha,
file-scope manifest, changed files, repo index, working-tree hash, green-run
attestation, and the F3 full-suite execution cwd) against the **local
checkout at the launch cwd** (`TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT`). The merge gate
(`_integrate_into_dev`, SA-0MT456M27001LRTL) and the stale-audit-base guard
(`_audit_base_freshness`, SA-0MT9EK1UU000DT1R) both integrate/verify against
`origin/dev`, but the pipeline still EXECUTES against the launch checkout.

Observed failure (2026-11-06, audit of RISE-0MW19AROF0035FRH in
tce-the-rising): the main checkout's `dev` branch carried a **local-only,
un-pushed, in-flight commit** (`d538e51`, RISE-0MW3GUQKX004W74K) that
modified `risingMatchHarness.ts`/`src/TheRisingAdversary.ts`, and was 6
commits *behind* `origin/dev`. The F3 full-suite gate ran `npm test` in that
contaminated checkout, failed on four integration suites (all import the
changed harness), and produced `Ready to close: No` with AC8 partial on an
item whose own scope was green at its tip. The merge gate passed because the
item's commits ARE ancestors of `origin/dev`; the stale-base guard passed
because they are also ancestors of the local HEAD — neither checks that
local HEAD == `origin/dev` or that there are no extra un-pushed commits.

The stale-audit-base guard only flags "delivered on origin/dev, absent from
local HEAD" (behind). It does not flag **ahead-with-extra-commits** (in-flight
work parked on the main checkout) or **aside** (local HEAD not an ancestor of
origin/dev), and it does not move execution into an isolated worktree.

## Users

- **Audit consumers (producers, implement agents)** — want an audit verdict
  that reflects the state of merged, checked-in dev — never a developer's
  un-pushed local experiments parked on the main checkout.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The audit runner resolves a **fresh, detached worktree at the latest
   `origin/dev`** (fetched before worktree creation) as the execution base
   for the full-suite green-run gate (F3) — the suite runs from that
   worktree, never from the launch checkout — and the worktree is removed
   afterward.
2. The stale-audit-base guard is extended to also abort (with the same loud
   remediation message) when the launch checkout is **ahead of /
   divergent from** `origin/dev` (local HEAD contains commits not in
   `origin/dev`), since an audit must never run against un-pushed in-flight
   work; a launch from a clean worktree of the owning repo stays valid.
3. Where feasible without changing verdict semantics, Phase 1/2 file-scope
   content (manifest, changed-file list, repo index, working-tree hash) also
   resolves against the origin/dev worktree rather than the launch checkout,
   so evidence never reflects a stale/dirty tree.
4. AC1–AC3 are covered by tests using a local bare "remote" with a dirty
   local checkout ahead of origin/dev (an un-pushed commit touching a
   harness file) — asserting the audit refuses/isolates rather than emitting
   misleading `partial`/`No` verdicts.
5. Existing behaviour is unchanged for a clean launch (launch checkout at
   origin/dev, worktree launches, `--do-not-persist`, batch/issue modes,
   `--no-execute`, child in-main-slot screens).
6. Documentation: audit skill reference (`docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`)
   and the audit SKILL.md are updated to state that audits execute inside a
   fresh origin/dev worktree and never against a stale/dirty launch checkout.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — base resolution for F3 suite
  execution, file-scope manifest, and the stale-audit-base guard.
- `skill/audit/scripts/test_cache.py` — cache keys are cwd-scoped; executing
  in a worktree changes the cwd used for cache hits.
- `skill/audit/tests/` — existing runner unit tests (fresh-base + guard
  coverage to extend).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — docs.

## Related work

- `RISE-0MW19AROF0035FRH` (tce-the-rising) — the audit that exposed this
  gap (spurious AC8 partial from a dirty launch checkout).
- `RISE-0MW3GUQKX004W74K` (tce-the-rising) — the work item whose un-pushed
  commit contaminated the main checkout.
- SA-0MT9EK1UU000DT1R — the existing stale-audit-base guard (behind-only).

## Out of scope

- Enforcing "no commits on the main checkout" (that is implement-skill
  hygiene, tracked elsewhere); this item only makes the audit robust to it.
- Changing the merge gate's integration semantics (that is already
  worktree-isolated at origin/dev).
- Verdict semantics, prompts, or the freshness/content-fingerprint gates.

discovered-from: WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG (ContextHub)

## Observed

While driving the ContextHub epic WL-0MW51OB1Y0073TLG (5 children) with `implement.py drive` (headless transport), the first driven child (WL-0MW55V82X009JYRV) hit a red changed-scope gate caused by a pre-existing, environment-only test failure (a hyphenated `TMPDIR`, tracked separately as WL-0MW5C6XS00071DWN). Instead of stopping after triage, the child:

1. created a brand-new work item (WL-0MW5C6XS00071DWN) and ran `implement.py start` for it;
2. edited files inside that item's worktree — the child had been spawned with `IMPLEMENT_DRIVE_ACTIVE=1` and `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH=<its own worktree>`, yet it `cd`-ed into a sibling worktree and edited there (the worktree-placement guard did not fire because the sibling worktree is a legitimate linked worktree);
3. added a dependency edge from its own item onto the newly created one;
4. ran repeated full suites (`--scope full --force`) for ~20 minutes, triaging unrelated performance-test failures.

The driver was stopped by the operator, the spurious edge removed, and the epic finished serially by hand. No data was lost; one commit that the child produced in the sibling worktree was later completed properly.

## Why it matters

A driven child that writes outside its own worktree can race the session that owns that worktree, silently widen the epic's scope, and consume the host's test slots. The existing placement guard only detects 'work landed in the main checkout', not 'work landed in a *different* linked worktree'.

## Acceptance criteria

- A driven child refuses (or is refused) any write whose path resolves into a linked worktree other than `IMPLEMENT_WORKTREE_PATH`, with an actionable message naming both roots.
- A child whose `finish` gate is red because of a failure it did not introduce reports and stops (triage → work item), instead of starting that work item's implementation itself.
- Regression test: a simulated driven child that `cd`s into a sibling worktree is detected and the run fails closed (no status mutation of either item).

data.description:
## Goal

Write unit tests for `_evaluate_red_suite` — the verdict integration function that combines mode + classification + relatedness.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Strict mode tests
- Any single failure in strict mode → `blocked` with reason "strict mode"
- Unit + integration mix → `blocked`
- All unit, all unrelated → `blocked` (strict mode ignores relatedness)
- Empty failures list → not applicable (caller handles green)

### Permissive mode tests — excusal path
- All failures unit-classified + all unrelated → `excused` with per-failure evidence
- Single unrelated unit failure → `excused`

### Permissive mode tests — fail-closed path
- Permissive fail-closed cases: in permissive mode the audit still fails when (a) any failure is integration/end-to-end classified, (b) any unit failure is affected by the item's changes, or (c) relatedness is inconclusive and no baseline comparison can be performed; unit tests cover each case individually, plus the mixed case (one excusable + one blocking failure ⇒ audit fails).
- Any integration/e2e failure → `blocked` with reason "integration test failure"
- Any unit failure classified as affected → `blocked` with reason "affected by item changes"
- Any unit failure classified as inconclusive (no baseline or baseline inconclusive) → `blocked` with reason "relatedness inconclusive"
- Mixed: one excusable unit + one blocking integration → `blocked` with both reasons recorded
- Mixed: one excusable unit + one affected unit → `blocked` with both reasons recorded

### Verdict structure
- `excused` verdict carries per-failure classification, relatedness, and evidence
- `blocked` verdict carries per-failure reasons
- Both verdicts include mode metadata

## Deliverables
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_strict_mode.py::TestVerdictIntegration`

## Key Files
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_strict_mode.py`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (new `_evaluate_red_suite`)

## Goal

Implement the failure classification and relatedness helper functions in `audit_runner.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `_classify_test_failure_scope(failure)` returns `"unit"` or `"integration"`:
   - Path convention: `tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` → `integration`
   - Everything else → `unit`
   - Unclassifiable (no path data) → `integration` (fail closed)

2. `_failure_relatedness(failure, touched_files, key_files, project_root)` returns `"affected"`, `"unrelated"`, or `"inconclusive"`:
   - Test file path ∈ changed files → `affected`
   - Module imported by test file ∈ changed files → `affected`
   - Changed file is shared test infrastructure (`conftest.py`, `tests/helpers/**`) → `affected`
   - No match → `inconclusive`

3. `_baseline_unrelated(failures, project_root, baseline_commit)` returns per-failure verdicts:
   - Creates scratch worktree at baseline commit (pre-change commit)
   - Runs only inconclusive failures through `paced_runner()` under `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` stand-down
   - Identical failure → `unrelated`; Pass → `affected`
   - Any baseline failure → `affected` (fail closed)
   - Any baseline error (worktree add, merge-base unresolvable, test absent) → `affected` (fail closed, no crash)
   - Never executes the main checkout; never recurses into nested suite runs

4. Scope classification and relatedness algorithm: failures are classified by path convention (`tests/integration/**`, `tests/e2e/**`, `tests/manual/**`, `**/*_e2e*`, `**/*integration*` ⇒ integration/end-to-end; everything else ⇒ unit; unclassifiable ⇒ integration, fail closed). Relatedness is decided by deterministic mapping first (failing test file ∈ item's changed files; a module the test imports ∈ changed files; a changed shared test-infrastructure file such as `conftest.py`/`tests/helpers/**`), then — only for inconclusive failures — by a baseline re-run of just those failures in a scratch worktree at the item's pre-change commit (fails identically ⇒ unrelated; passes ⇒ affected). Unit tests cover the pattern table, the import-mapping step, and the baseline comparison (both outcomes), with no real suite execution.

5. No real suite execution in unit tests (mock `paced_runner` / subprocess)
6. Unit tests pass (see child test items)

## Deliverables
- `_classify_test_failure_scope()` — path-pattern classifier
- `_failure_relatedness()` — deterministic mapping + import scan
- `_baseline_unrelated()` — scratch worktree baseline re-run
- Error handling: never crashes, always returns `affected` for infrastructure failures

## Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (new functions)
